more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
No current country-wide food-use ban was confirmed in the regulatory sources checked in 2026.
The permissions checked in 2026 apply only to the specified preparations, food uses and conditions.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain cocoa and Chocolate products as covered by Directive 2000/36/EC; other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; fruit juices as defined by Directive 2001/112/EC and vegetable juices; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
more_info.origin: Hot water extracts the soluble polysaccharides from soybean fibre. Ethanol may be used to recover the refined material.
more_info.dietary_restrictions: The specified starting material is plant derived and compatible with vegetarian and vegan diets. The specification does not establish halal or kosher certification.
more_info.daily_intake: No numerical ADI needed for the assessed uses (EFSA, 2017).
more_info.side_effects:
Estimated actual food-use exposure was low and unlikely to raise concern.
EFSA identified residual soybean proteins as a potential allergen issue.
more_info.overview: Soybean hemicellulose is a refined water-soluble polysaccharide fraction extracted from soybean fibre. Hot water extracts the soluble polysaccharides from soybean fibre. Ethanol may be used to recover the refined material. The specified material is supplied as white powder. EU permissions include processed eggs and egg products, food supplements supplied in a liquid form excluding food supplements for infants and young children.
